toegepas.rede_vinder: An English word quoted as what someone calls a thing should be in quotation marks, which also shows it is not the lesson's own word.
toegepas.fout: The English word the children use is not marked as a cited word, so it reads as if it were the lesson's own term.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Quotation marks set off the borrowed English name without changing any word, and the protected word damptoestelle stays intact.

toegepas.blok: Wat middels aan die verstand doen
toegepas.voor: die brein vra dan harder daarvoor
toegepas.na: die brein vra dan sterker daarna
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Vra harder daarvoor' sounds like a translation of 'asks harder for it'; Afrikaans says 'vra na' and 'sterker' for a stronger craving.
toegepas.fout: 'Vra harder daarvoor' copies English 'asks harder for it', and 'harder' can be read as 'louder'.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Die brein vra dan sterker daarna' is the natural Afrikaans expression for a craving, and the brain still wants the same thing.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Rondom' is more natural than 'langs' for people near a smoker who breathe in the smoke; 'langs' suggests only someone right beside them.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: A preposition swap that widens 'beside the smoker' to 'all around the smoker' changes the scope of a health claim, and the original reads naturally.

laat_vaar.voor: Party mense sukkel om op te hou en
laat_vaar.na: Party mense sukkel om op te hou drink en
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Om op te hou' has no object here; 'op te hou drink' says clearly what they struggle to stop, without adding content.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The alcohol paragraph already supplies the object, the same bare 'om op te hou' is used in the tobacco paragraph and the list, and a bare 'drink' could read as any drink.

laat_vaar.blok: Medisyne wat jy sonder 'n dokter se brief koop
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Medisyne drink' is colloquial and does not fit pills; 'gebruik' is the standard verb and covers all medicine.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Medisyne drink' is idiomatic Afrikaans for taking medicine, and 'gebruik' widens the misuse example and repeats 'gebruik' from the previous sentence.

na_skrywer.blok: Wat jy doen as iemand jou iets aanbied
na_skrywer.voor: want die skool en die kliniek help
na_skrywer.na: want die skool en die kliniek kan help
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: Bare 'help' at the end of the sentence sounds unfinished; 'kan help' is the natural way to say they are there to help.
na_skrywer.fout: A bare 'help' at the end of the sentence sounds unfinished.
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: The sentence is the reason given in the lesson's safety instruction about who to tell, and 'kan help' also changes 'they help' into 'they are able to help', so the writer should decide the wording.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: The sentence before has 'Party kinders' as its subject, so 'Hulle' can at first read as the children rather than the damptoestelle; meaning is clear from 'bevat', so this is only a note, and 'Damptoestelle bevat meestal ook nikotien' would remove it if a person agrees.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Medisyne wat jy sonder 'n dokter se brief koop
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Medisyne soos iets vir hoofpyn koop 'n mens by 'n apteek sonder 'n dokter se brief.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: 'n Mens koop medisyne soos iets vir hoofpyn sonder 'n dokter se brief by 'n apteek.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Fronting the object makes the sentence hard to parse at first reading; subject-first order is clearer for Grade 5.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Fronting the object to match the heading is normal Afrikaans and reads clearly with 'n mens' straight after, so the reorder is a lateral move.
